prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where a new temple was dedicated from 1987 through 1998 (not counting rededications).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory where a new temple was dedicated from 1987 through 1998 (not counting rededications).
prompts.summary: Only five countries and territories saw a new temple dedicated from 1987 through 1998: Frankfurt in 1987, Toronto in 1990, Hong Kong in 1996 and Preston, England, in 1998, plus nine in the United States. The wave of smaller temples began with Monticello, Utah, in 1998.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Bountiful Utah, 1995; Las Vegas Nevada, 1989; Monticello Utah, 1998; and 6 more.

answers.fact: Toronto Ontario, 1990.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Frankfurt Germany, 1987.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Preston England, 1998.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: Hong Kong China, 1996.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding Tyre, Zidon, Philistia, Egypt or Edom, judged in Joel 3, or Greece, where Judah's children were sold
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land the Lord calls to account in Joel 3 (Tyre, Zidon, the coasts of Palestine, Egypt, Edom), or Greece, where Judah's children were sold
prompts.summary: Joel 3 rebukes Tyre, Zidon and the Philistine coast for selling the children of Judah to the Grecians, and says Judah will in turn sell their children to the Sabeans, an Arab tribe. It also foretells desolation for Egypt and Edom, while Judah and Jerusalem endure forever (Joel 3:19-20).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Egypt shall be a desolation (Joel 3:19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The coasts of Palestine, the Philistine shore, held Ashkelon and Ashdod (Joel 3:4).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Tyre and Zidon are rebuked for selling the children of Judah (Joel 3:4).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom shall be a desolate wilderness (Joel 3:19).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The Philistine coast of Joel 3:4 also held Gaza, now in the Gaza Strip.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Judah's children were sold unto the Grecians (Joel 3:6).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the United States that Gordon B. Hinckley visited in 1998
prompts.text_original: In 1998 President Gordon B. Hinckley traveled about 77,000 miles to meet Saints around the world. A country outside the United States that he visited that year.
prompts.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley logged about 77,000 miles in 1998. In February he toured West, East and Southern Africa, announcing a temple in Accra and stopping in Cape Verde and the Canary Islands. He also visited northern Mexico, western Europe including Preston, England, 13 Canadian stops, and in November Nicaragua and Honduras.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where German, the language of an 1852 Book of Mormon translation, is an official language today.
prompts.text_original: The German translation of the Book of Mormon was published in Hamburg in 1852, one of the earliest translations. Pin a country where German is an official language today.
prompts.summary: The German Book of Mormon came out in Hamburg in May 1852, with a special edition carrying French and German on facing pages. German is official today in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Luxembourg and Liechtenstein, so that 1852 translation still serves members in six countries.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: The German Book of Mormon was published in Hamburg on May 25, 1852.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: German is the official language of Austria.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: German is one of four national languages; the Swiss chronology records the 1852 German edition.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: German is one of Belgium's three official languages; its chronology records the 1852 German edition.

answers.name: Luxembourg
answers.fact: German is one of Luxembourg's three official languages.

answers.name: Liechtenstein
answers.fact: German is the official language of Liechtenstein.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where French, given a Book of Mormon translation in 1852, is an official language as of October 2026.
prompts.text_original: The first French Book of Mormon was published in 1852, during John Taylor's mission to France. Today French is an official language across much of Africa. Pin an African country where French is an official language as of October 2026.
prompts.citation: Global Histories: France chronology (1852); official-language status is general knowledge
prompts.summary: The French Book of Mormon was first published in 1852, within two years of John Taylor opening France. That early translation now reaches far beyond France: French is an official or working language in about twenty African countries, from Senegal and Ivory Coast to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar.
